goal:
Make `mergeConfig` in `src/config.js` merge nested plain objects key by key, at any depth: `mergeConfig({ server: { host: "localhost", port: 8080 } }, { server: { port: 9090 } })` returns `{ server: { host: "localhost", port: 9090 } }`.

Keep everything that works today. An override value that is not a plain object, such as an array, `null`, a string, or a number, replaces the default value whole, as it does now: `mergeConfig({ tags: ["a", "b"] }, { tags: ["c"] })` returns `{ tags: ["c"] }`. `mergeConfig` never modifies its arguments.

constraints: Change as few files as possible.
Delete or simplify existing code before you add code.
Write a failing test that reproduces the problem before you change any source file.

challengers.defect: Null-prototype plain objects are misclassified as non-plain objects and replaced whole instead of recursively merged.
Null-prototype plain objects are not recognized as plain objects, so they are replaced instead of recursively merged.

candidates.approach: Implement recursive, copy-on-write merging directly in src/config.js. Start each merge with the existing object-spread behavior, then recursively replace result entries where both corresponding values are plain objects. Treat objects with Object.prototype or null prototypes as plain, and leave arrays, null, primitives, and class instances as whole-value replacements. Allocate a new object for each merged branch without modifying either input, and retain spread semantics for enumerable own string and symbol keys.
candidates.firstStep: Add node:test regression cases for the supplied examples, three-level nesting, non-plain replacement values, and frozen inputs before changing mergeConfig.

candidates.approach: Use an explicit work stack instead of recursion. In src/config.js, create the root result using object spread and enqueue pairs of plain-object branches with their destination objects; process those frames until every eligible nested branch is merged. This explores an iterative implementation that avoids call-stack exhaustion on deeply nested configurations while retaining whole-value replacement for other values and allocating all merged containers independently of the inputs.
candidates.firstStep: Write a deep-nesting test and sketch stack frames containing defaults, overrides, and the destination object, with only enumerable own override keys eligible for traversal.

candidates.approach: Delegate nested merging to a maintained merge library through a compatibility adapter, rather than building the traversal locally. Add the dependency and keep mergeConfig as a thin wrapper that preserves its existing root object-spread behavior. Configure or adapt the library so recursion occurs only between plain objects, arrays and other non-plain overrides replace wholesale, and inputs remain untouched. This is less attractive for such a small module, but explores reuse; reject a library if its key handling or replacement semantics cannot satisfy the compatibility tests.
candidates.firstStep: Create a compatibility test matrix covering arrays, null, explicit undefined, symbol keys, null-prototype objects, class instances, and immutable inputs, then evaluate a candidate merge library against it.

candidates.approach: Separate planning from application using immutable path-based updates. Traverse the two configurations to collect replacement operations, descending only when both values at a key are plain objects; apply those operations to the root spread result by copying each affected ancestor before updating it. Use arrays of property keys rather than dotted strings so literal dots and symbols remain valid keys. This is more elaborate than direct recursion, but explores a patch-oriented strategy with independently testable change discovery and application.
candidates.firstStep: Prototype an internal patch collector and test that a nested port override produces a replacement path while an array override produces one whole-value replacement operation.
